messages:
ryan: Heads-up — CI started failing for the flash_paged kernel target after #3421 landed. Linking errors during the shared lib step. Error snippet below, full log at the CI job link.

maya: saw that too from the nightly bench run, also observed a latency spike on paged/fused variants for seq_len >= 4096. Possibly related.

sam: paste of the exact linker error:
```
/usr/bin/ld: fused_attention.o: in function `init_flash_ops':
fused_attention.cu:(.text+0x1a3): undefined reference to `flash_attn_unfused_v2'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

li: my first guess is a toolchain mismatch between the build container and the dev image we compile locally. We've seen LTO/visibility issues cause missing symbol exports before. Which compiler and flags are the CI builders using?

devops-bot: CI job failed: https://ci.internal/rdw/12345 (build/flash_paged/linux-x86_64) — exit code 1. Re-run button available.

maya: repro steps that failed for me locally:
```
docker run --rm -it --entrypoint /bin/bash redwood/builder:base-2024-10
git checkout feature/flash-paged && bazel build //runtime/kernels:flash_paged --config=release
```
Link fails inside `bazel-bin/runtime/libredwood_kernels.so`.

aj: quick triage — the symbol name `flash_attn_unfused_v2` is compiled when we enable FLASH_V2 and BUILD_FUSED=true. If the fused target is built with -flto and the unfused is in another object with different visibility or different C++ abi flags (-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI), the linker can drop it. CI image change in #3398 switched base image to ubuntu:22.04 + gcc12, while our local builder still uses gcc11.

sam: suggests workaround: force the kernel targets to use `-fno-lto` and `-fvisibility=default` for the shared lib build. We can also add an explicit `__attribute__((used))` on the registration entry to avoid it being optimized away.

emma: perf context — bench-bot's nightly: fused attention P99 increased ~7% for seq_len 8192 on A100; the fallback changed to unfused for some shapes which pushes more load on batching heuristics. If we revert the ordering change in kernel selector, perf comes back to baseline.

li: if it's both a symbol export and a perf regression, my vote is two-pronged: (1) patch the build to be robust to LTO/toolchain differences (disable LTO on kernel objects, enforce -fPIC), (2) revert the selector change that triggered the unfused fallback for large seq_len and re-run benches.

ryan: agreed. @alex-infra can you roll a new builder image that pins gcc 11 toolchain for the release branch and include glibc headers that match the runners? We need parity between CI and local images to avoid these link-time surprises.

alex-infra: I can cut a patch image. ETA ~2 hours. I'll add a test that runs a tiny link-smoke test after compile (load libredwood_kernels.so and check exported symbol list). Any preferred tooling?

aj: LD_PRELOAD sanity check + `nm -D libredwood_kernels.so | grep flash_attn_unfused_v2` as part of smoke is fine. Also add a simple nightly bench gate that fails if fused perf regresses >3% on target shapes.

emma: I'll add a bench case for seq_len 4096/8192 and a synthetic workload that exercises paged KV. Bench-bot will post results to #bench-results.

sam: immediate short-term fix: revert the kernel selector ordering change in the runtime (it's small) and open a follow-up to reintroduce after addressing toolchain/linker hardening. I can PR that now.

ryan: sounds good. Plan: 1) sam PR revert (short-lived) 2) alex builds new image with gcc11 and smoke tests 3) aj pushes CFLAGS fixes (-fno-lto, -fPIC) for kernel builds 4) emma adds bench gate 5) re-enable selector once toolchain issues proven fixed.

devops-bot: CI re-run queued by @alex-infra: https://ci.internal/rdw/12346

bench-bot: nightly bench snapshot attached: paged/fused comparison: fused baseline 1.00 -> current 1.07 (P99). Full CSV in artifact 98765.

ryan: thanks everyone. Please post updates here. If anyone finds a smaller repro (single-file C++/CUDA) with the symbol drop, drop it in this thread so infra can reproduce outside bazel.

maya: quick note — keep an eye on KV cache behavior while testing; we saw a small throughput dip when kernel selector changed for 2-segment cache hits. Might be a separate tuning issue but flagging it now.

li: will follow-up on KV cache traces and add a couple of microbenchmarks to isolate caching vs kernel selection impact.

ryan: closing loop — I'll create a checklist in the PR description summarizing steps and link back here.
